metadata.author: James F. Walters

stages.name: Stage 2: Monograph Core Framework & Residuum Calculus
Stage 3: The Five Foundational Anchor Witnesses
Stage 4: Advanced Synthesis, Lean Formalization & Research Horizons

nodes.label: Classical Logic & Proof Theory
nodes.description: Syntax, semantics, soundness, completeness, first-order theories, Peano arithmetic, and classical reverse mathematics (RCA_0).

nodes.label: Abstract Algebra (Groups, Rings, Modules)
nodes.description: Groups, rings, fields, ideals, quotient structures, modules over commutative rings, homomorphisms, and exact sequences.

nodes.label: Point-Set Topology
nodes.description: Topological spaces, open/closed sets, continuity, compactness, connectedness, Hausdorff separation (T_2), and product topologies.

nodes.label: Posets, Lattices & Choice
nodes.description: Partially ordered sets, complete lattices, Heyting algebras, Boolean algebras, Zorn's Lemma, and the Axiom of Choice (AC).

nodes.label: Computability & Recursion Theory
nodes.description: Turing machines, computable partial functions, decidability, halting problem, Kleene S-m-n theorem, and Turing reducibility.

nodes.label: Real Analysis & Metric Spaces
nodes.description: Metric spaces, Cauchy sequences, completeness, Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT), Extreme Value Theorem (EVT), and Heine-Borel compactness.

nodes.label: First-Course Category Theory
nodes.description: Categories, functors, natural transformations, limits and colimits, adjunctions, and universal properties.

nodes.label: Presheaves & Yoneda Lemma
nodes.description: Presheaf category Set^(C^op), Yoneda embedding, representability, and colimits of representable presheaves.

nodes.label: Lawvere Theories & Algebras
nodes.description: Categories with finite products representing algebraic theories, models in arbitrary categories, and algebraic functors.

nodes.label: 2-Categories & 2-Monadic Doctrines
nodes.description: 2-categories, 2-functors, monads on categories, algebras for a monad, and 2-monadic doctrines over Cat.

nodes.label: Chain Complexes & Homological Algebra
nodes.description: Additive and abelian categories, chain complexes, homology, exact sequences, Snake Lemma, and 5-lemma.

nodes.label: Sheaves on Topological Spaces
nodes.description: Presheaves of rings/modules, sheaf gluing condition, stalks, germs, and sheafification.

nodes.label: Elementary Topoi & Subobject Classifier
nodes.description: Cartesian closed categories with finite limits, subobject classifier Omega, power objects, and internal logic.

nodes.label: Simplicial Sets & Model Categories
nodes.description: Simplex category Delta, simplicial sets Set^(Delta^op), Kan complexes, horn filling, and geometric realization.

nodes.label: Lawvere Hyperdoctrines
nodes.description: First-order logic as adjoints to substitution (exists_f -| f^* -| forall_f), Beck-Chevalley condition, and equality predicates.

nodes.label: Derived Categories & Spectral Sequences
nodes.description: Derived functors Ext and Tor, triangulated categories, derived category D(A), and Grothendieck-Leray spectral sequences.

nodes.label: Affine Schemes (Spec R)
nodes.description: Prime spectrum of a commutative ring, Zariski topology, structure sheaf O_Spec(R), and localization at prime ideals.

nodes.label: Grothendieck Topologies & Sites
nodes.description: Covering sieves, Grothendieck topologies J, axioms for a site (C, J), and sheaves on a site.

nodes.label: Internal Logic & Kripke-Joyal Semantics
nodes.description: Mitchell-Bénabou language, internal interpretation of connectives and quantifiers, and Kripke-Joyal sheaf forcing.

nodes.label: General Schemes & Locally Ringed Spaces
nodes.description: Locally ringed spaces, morphisms of locally ringed spaces, gluing affine schemes, and relative schemes.

nodes.label: Grothendieck Topoi & Geometric Morphisms
nodes.description: Sheaves on a site, Giraud's theorem, geometric morphisms f = (f^* -| f_*), and bounded geometric morphisms.

nodes.label: Triposes & Realizability Topoi (RT/Eff)
nodes.description: Partial combinatory algebras (PCAs), Hyland's tripos-to-topos construction, and the Effective Topos Eff = RT(K_1).

nodes.label: (inf, 1)-Categories & Quasicategories
nodes.description: Joyal quasicategories, Lurie's HTT, higher limits and colimits, and Grothendieck (inf, 1)-topoi.

nodes.label: Stable (inf, 1)-Categories & Spectra
nodes.description: Zero objects, fiber/cofiber sequences, suspension-loop equivalence Sigma = Omega, and spectrum objects Sp.

nodes.label: Weak Set Subsystems & Class Theories (ETCS, ZC, NBG)
nodes.description: Two-sorted Bernays-Godel and Kelley-Morse class theories (GB_0, GBC, NBG, ETR_omega proving Con(ZFC), ETR_Ord, KM) and CT^-[ZFC] with Godel operations G1-G8, Mac Lane set theory (Mac ~= ETCS) vs. Zermelo ZC vs. ZFC^-, and Gale-Stewart Borel games.

nodes.label: Endofunctor Coalgebras, Bisimulation & Truncations
nodes.description: Initial algebras (mu F) vs. terminal coalgebras (nu F), Lambek's isomorphism, accessible pointed graphs (APGs) and maximum bisimulation, quotient types (Quot.sound), and (-1)- vs. 0-truncations in univalent universes.

nodes.label: CRM Paradigm: Geometry Over Syntax
nodes.description: Transitioning reverse mathematics from syntactic arithmetic (RCA_0) to structural, topological, and cohomological geometry of doctrines.

nodes.label: Categorical Doctrine (D in Doct)
nodes.description: 2-monadic and hyperdoctrinal specifications of mathematical universes equipped with operations, limits, and quantifiers.

nodes.label: Doctrinal Comparison Triple (T)
nodes.description: Tuple T = (D_0 >= D_1, kappa: Phi => Psi) induced by a comparison square alpha and its mutually inverse Beck-Chevalley mate mu_alpha in a Grothendieck doctrinal fibration p : E -> B.

nodes.label: Categorical Residuum Operator (Res)
nodes.description: Truncated Homotopy-Fiber Defect ||hofib_y(F_X)||_n and Res(kappa), with Modes (i)-(iii) (internal vs. external section splitting, specified J-completion phantoms, and rigidified vs. Aut(B)-orbit forgetful lifts), calibrated via Doctrinal Philosophies P = (D, P) and the four-family Admissibility Criterion.

nodes.label: Fundamental Equivalence of CRM
nodes.description: The foundational equivalence D_0 + Res(kappa) <=> D_1 asserting exact gap calibration by the residuum.

nodes.label: Topos-Logical Relative Pseudocomplement
nodes.description: Residuum specialization (A =>_Topos B) acting as an order-theoretic relative pseudocomplement in universe lattices.

nodes.label: Axis I: Choice / Splitting Coordinate Axis
nodes.description: External AC, internal IAC, COSHEP, WISC, SVC, Diaconescu theorem, and projectivity of 1_E.

nodes.label: Axis II: Constructive Logic & Omega-Geometry
nodes.description: Geometry of subobject classifier: De Morgan Stone lattices, Gödel-Dummett linearity, and Boolean collapse Omega = 1+1.

nodes.label: Axis III: Arithmetic Infinity & Rigidity
nodes.description: NNO existence, finite dynamical lassos, Dedekind vs Kuratowski infinity, and biproduct tail cokernels.

nodes.label: Axis IV: Characteristic & p-Torsion
nodes.description: Joyal p-typical delta-rings, lift torsors, relative slice perfection A -> A_perf, and polynomial cofactors.

nodes.label: Axis V: Directional Invertibility & Higher Cells
nodes.description: Invertibility spectra, cellular directed complexes, 4-tier ladder, and categorical spectra CatSp.

nodes.label: Two-Axis Relativization Framework
nodes.description: Axis 1 (ambient fiber deformation) vs Axis 2 (metamathematical base deformation gamma: E -> S); absolute vs relative residua.

nodes.label: Base-Fiber Conservation Principle
nodes.description: Order-theoretic and cohomological base-fiber strength conservation (4-term Giraud torsor-gerbe / 5-term Leray sequence, Choice-slice and SVC forcing).

nodes.label: Axis VI: Quotient-Image Descent & Small-Map AST (C, S)
nodes.description: Joyal-Moerdijk predicative class-set ambients (C, S), contravariant small powerclasses P_S, pointillist continuum H(aleph_1) |= ZFC^-, CZF Omega^X / 2^X split, and Axis VI quotient-image descent im(f) in S.

nodes.label: Axis VII: Foundation vs. Anti-Foundation (Coalg_wf -> Coalg)
nodes.description: Axis VII coalgebra-doctrine comparison Coalg_wf(P_S) -> Coalg(P_S) inducing strict kappa_Reg : nu^wf P_S ~= mu P_S -> nu P_S (separating well-founded V_ZF from Aczel's V_AFA and Quine atom q = {q}), Friedman's IZF_non-ext quotient cost, and Gylterud's hereditary (-1)-truncation V_0 -> mu P_Anima.

nodes.label: Witness I: Parity Torsor T_odd in Nom
nodes.description: Odd-finset parity torsor [T_odd] = delta(1) != 0 in H^1(Nom; EvenFinset) witnessing non-projectivity of 1_Nom and AC failure.

nodes.label: Witness II: 2-Torsion delta-Ring R_2 & DualInt
nodes.description: R_2 = Z[eta]/(2eta, eta^2) with delta_0(eta)=0, delta_1(eta)=eta and DualInt = Z[eps]/(eps^2) pinning relative slice perfection.

nodes.label: Witness III: Gaunt Step-Product Q & Phantom
nodes.description: Noetherian rank-omega step-product Q in prod A_k with pure Postnikov phantom X_bullet in RL(Q) \ Q disproving Conjecture C1.

nodes.label: Witness IV: Directed Facet Cycles F_3 / F_n
nodes.description: Facet-supported directed triangle F_3 = partial Delta^2 and F_n = partial Delta^(n-1) erecting the n >= 3 cubical amalgamation wall.

nodes.label: Witness V: Light Condensed Q_E0 & UHF(2^inf)
nodes.description: Light condensed Cantor tail quotient Q_E0 = 2^N // E0 with UHF(2^inf) and presentation class [q] != 0 in Ext^1_CondAb_light, with Borel-coding bridge to radial exotic R^4 announcements.

nodes.label: Seven Multi-Dimensional Non-AC Lattices
nodes.description: Continuum trichotomy, pointfree/spatial duality (Tychonoff, Hahn-Banach), homological exactness bifurcation, and Categorical Big Five.

nodes.label: Higher Choice AC_(n,m) & Postnikov Gerbes
nodes.description: Bigraded higher choice, un-truncated choice collapse, Postnikov gerbe obstructions, and Postnikov completeness vs. hypercompleteness.

nodes.label: Choice-Geometry Residuum Atlas
nodes.description: Complete classification of Barr-Diaconescu-Freyd, Internal-to-External choice, COSHEP-SVC, and localic decompositions.

nodes.label: Site Combinatorics & Kihara Atomic Spectrum
nodes.description: Fraïssé permutation topoi Cont(G), 5-rung atomic choice spectrum, Lawvere-Tierney subtopoi, and Weihrauch degrees.

nodes.label: Four-Tier (inf, inf)-Ladder & Hom-Rank
nodes.description: Strict chain Cat^L subset Cat^omega subset Cat^coind subset Cat^R, ordinal hom-rank, and LALI ceiling +2.

nodes.label: Cubical Disjoint n-Amalgamation Dichotomy
nodes.description: Two-clause flow-convex embeddings (IsFlowConvex), minimal-support amalgams, and higher n-amalgamation phase transition.

nodes.label: The Five Core Conjectures of CRM
nodes.description: Five program-defining conjectures: Cohomological Vanishing (proved on top, IBPI, IDC, SVC), Etale omega-Presentability, Stone/Profinite Isotropy, Postnikov Stepwise Effacement (proved for n >= 1, liens, nilpotent bands & etale R(E_1) splitting), and Two-Sorted Big-Five Adjoint/Fixed-Point Hierarchy.

nodes.label: Categorical Spectra CatSp & Stabilization
nodes.description: CatSp = Sp(Cat^R_*), directed loop-suspension stabilization without Wall diffeomorphism or Giraud initiality collapse.

nodes.label: Double-Solvent Theorem for 4-Smoothings
nodes.description: Double-Solvent Theorem on light-condensed E_0 tail quotient Q_E0 = [2^N // F_2^{<omega}] and Connes groupoid G_E0, with Borel-coding bridge to radial exotic R^4's and Freedman collapse.

nodes.label: Class Kaleidoscope Def -| pi_Set & GC Non-Conservativity
nodes.description: Coreflective baseline Def -| pi_Set, Williams's fixed-set class kaleidoscope, skeletal splitting Card -> Set <=> GC, CT^-[ZFC] vs. ETR_Ord (Con(ZFC)) vs. KM, LoS <=> Rep & GC, V_(omega+omega) colimit escape, and Glazer's ZC non-conservativity.

nodes.label: Boffa Hyperset Torsors & Univalent nu P_Anima Loops
nodes.description: Boffa hypersets V_BAFA, non-isomorphic bisimulation fibers (2-cycle vs. q), Rieger-Bernays slice twin [Q_0^(2)] and global parity [T_odd(Q_0)] torsors, and sequential-limit M-types nu P_Anima (Omega(nu P_Anima, q) ~= 1, Omega(nu P_Anima, [q, q]) ~= Z/2Z) uniting Axes V and VII.

nodes.label: Double-Clamped Set_ZFC Scale-Invariance & SetsResiduum
nodes.description: Borel determinacy pincer (ZFC^- unprovability at Sigma^0_4 in minimal/non-standard beta-models lacking P(N) vs. ZC unprovability at Sigma^0_omega and colimit escape in V_(omega+omega)), reflexive scale-invariance pinching 1-categorical AST (C, S) into Set_ZFC via Osius pure-set fullness & well-pointedness (bridging to (X, U_0 in U_1)), and SetsResiduum.lean kernel separation (propext, choice, Quot.sound).

nodes.label: Lean 4 HomotopyCRM Production Ledger
nodes.description: Four-layer Lean 4 honesty gate and eleven-module production verification suite (22,016 lines, 234 #print axioms checks across InfinityResiduum, DeltaRingPerfection, BorelTailResiduum, OrdinalRankCompleteness, StepProductPhantom, DirectedFraisseSAP, NominalSimplicity, CubicalAmalgamation, NominalICaTT, SetsResiduum, and DoctrinalFibration).

nodes.label: 17 Open Problems across Eight Horizons
nodes.description: Seventeen open research problems across Horizons I-VIII: Pareto residuum frontiers, Weihrauch-Lawvere-Tierney duality, Kihara higher-cardinal stability, cubical phase transitions, Postnikov representation 1-gerbes, CatSp stabilization, exotic R^4 condensations, Borel determinacy class coalgebras, class calibration of the (inf, inf)-ladder, and pi_Set transgression.

nodes.label: Epilogue: Truth as Obstruction Invariant
nodes.description: Master 27-row Reference Atlas across Axes I-VII, reflexive scale-invariance of double-clamped Set_ZFC inside (C, S) bridging to univalent (X, U) and Volume II (C_inf, S_inf), the five anchor witnesses, and truth as universal obstruction invariant.

edges.rationale: Order-theoretic structures formalize logical consequence and lattice operations.
Computability formalizes effective proof procedures and formal systems.
First-order predicate logic is the structural content modeled by hyperdoctrines.
First-order vs. two-sorted set/class syntax and Separation/Replacement schemata build on classical predicate logic.
Classical reverse mathematics provides the baseline paradigm being generalized.
Concrete algebraic categories (Grp, Ring, Mod) motivate abstract categorical axioms.
Universal algebra signatures and equational laws define Lawvere theories.
Modules and module homomorphisms are the basic objects of homological complexes.
Commutative rings and prime ideals form the foundational carrier of Spec R.
Point-set topological properties ground convergence, compactness, and metric continuity.
Sheaf condition is defined on open sets of a topological space.
Geometric realization links combinatorial simplices to topological spaces.
Cantor/Baire tree topologies ground Gale-Stewart infinite games and Borel determinacy payoff ranks.
Posets and thin categories provide the primary bridge to abstract category theory.
Subobject lattices and power objects generalize Boolean and Heyting algebras.
Lattices of predicates form the fiber categories in Lawvere hyperdoctrines.
Von Neumann ordinals, cumulative ranks V_alpha, and well-ordering Choice anchor ZC, ZFC^-, and NBG.
Partial combinatory algebras (PCAs) formalize Turing computability categorically.
Recursion theory grounds the arithmetic hierarchy and NNO finitary rigidity.
Classical real analysis theorems (IVT, EVT, Cauchy) form the non-AC testbed.
Presheaves are contravariant functors from a base category to Set.
Lawvere theories are categories with finite products.
Monads and 2-categories build directly on categorical adjunctions and functor categories.
Additive and abelian categories formalize exact sequences and homology.
Topoi are Cartesian closed categories with finite limits and subobject classifiers.
Hyperdoctrines are functors from a base category to Poset/Heyting.
Endofunctor F-algebras, F-coalgebras, and Lambek's isomorphism are formulated via universal arrows.
Sheaves are presheaves satisfying the local gluing condition.
Presheaf categories Set^(C^op) form the prototype elementary topos.
Simplicial sets are presheaves on the simplex category Delta.
Sieves on a category are subfunctors of representable presheaves.
Lawvere theories provide the algebraic base and functorial semantics for categorical hyperdoctrines.
Functorial semantics of algebraic theories formalizes categorical doctrines (D in Doct).
2-monadic doctrines formalize the universe classes across which CRM operates.
Doctrines in CRM are formalized as 2-monadic algebras or hyperdoctrines.
Derived categories inverting quasi-isomorphisms build on chain complexes.
Spec R is equipped with the structure sheaf of localized rings.
Grothendieck sites generalize topological spaces to categories with coverage.
The subobject classifier Omega interprets the Mitchell-Bénabou internal logic.
Every Grothendieck topos is an elementary topos with colimits and a site.
Realizability topoi are elementary topoi constructed via tripos fibrations.
Cole-Mitchell-Osius bi-interpretability identifies Lawvere's Boolean elementary-topos ETCS with Mac Lane set theory (Mac).
Power-object coalgebras, internal equivalence relations, and subobject monomorphisms generalize set membership.
Quasicategories are simplicial sets satisfying inner horn filling conditions.
The facet complex F_n = partial Delta^(n-1) is a combinatorial simplicial sphere.
Adjoint quantifiers in hyperdoctrines ground internal topos logic.
Categorical doctrines generalize Lawvere hyperdoctrines to arbitrary universes.
Derived categories are the homotopy categories of stable (inf, 1)-categories.
The 5-term Grothendieck-Leray sequence comes from spectral sequences of derived functors.
General schemes are locally ringed spaces obtained by gluing affine schemes.
Delta-rings and Frobenius lifts operate natively on affine schemes and their rings.
Spec R_2 and Spec DualInt are concrete affine schemes exhibiting lift obstructions.
A Grothendieck topos is the category of sheaves on a Grothendieck site.
Kripke-Joyal semantics generalize to realizability interpretation in Eff.
Internal choice IAC is expressed directly in the internal Mitchell-Bénabou language.
Omega-geometry determines the intuitionistic vs classical truth values internally.
Relative schemes X -> S provide the geometric foundation for two-axis relativization and fibered category base-change.
Schemes and locally ringed spaces provide geometric models for synthetic differential geometry (Lattice VI) and localic spectrum constructions.
Grothendieck (inf, 1)-topoi are the higher-categorical generalization of Grothendieck topoi.
Geometric morphisms between Grothendieck topoi calibrate the relative pseudocomplement.
Base-topos variation relies on bounded geometric morphisms gamma: E -> S.
Nominal topos Nom is a Grothendieck topos of continuous G-sets.
The effective topos Eff houses realizability residuums for WKL and FAN.
Stable (inf, 1)-categories are (inf, 1)-categories with zero objects and exact triangles.
Homotopy (-1)- and 0-truncations and loop groups pi_1(M, x) ~= Aut(x) require univalent (inf, 1)-categories.
Directional invertibility and cell stabilization operate in (inf, 1)-categories.
Step-product Q is an (inf, inf)-category constructed from globular and complicial nerves.
Higher choice AC_(n,m) is formulated across truncation levels in (inf, 1)-topoi.
Categorical spectra CatSp generalize stable homotopy theory to directed categories.
Godel operations G1-G8 and weak subsystems (Mac, ZC, ZFC^-) motivate predicative AST ambients (C, S).
Two-sorted GB_0/GBC/NBG/KM hierarchies and Mac/ZC models underlie Def -| pi_Set and Glazer's non-conservativity.
Initial algebras, terminal APG coalgebras, and (-1)-truncation directly define V_ZF = mu P_S, V_AFA = nu P_S, and V_0 -> mu P_Anima.
Distinguishing APG in-isomorphism fibers from maximum bisimulation classes separates Boffa's V_BAFA from Aczel's V_AFA.
The CRM paradigm is formalized through the category of doctrines Doct.
Comparison triples compare an ambient doctrine D_0 with a subdoctrine D_1.
The residuum operator Res assigns an obstruction to each comparison triple.
The fundamental equivalence establishes D_0 + Res(kappa) <=> D_1.
Specializing the fundamental equivalence to topoi gives the relative pseudocomplement.
Axis I choice residua are computed via topos-logical relative pseudocomplements.
Axis II constructive logic residua classify subobject classifier degenerations.
Axis III arithmetic infinity residua measure finitary-to-infinitary doctrine gaps.
Axis IV characteristic residua measure Frobenius and delta-ring lift obstructions.
Axis V directional residua measure cell invertibility and stabilization barriers.
Axis VI calibrates small-map quotient-image descent im(f) in S as a doctrinal comparison residuum on (C, S).
Axis VII measures anti-cycle and anti-symmetry universe clamps via doctrinal comparison triples.
Choice principles deform non-trivially when relativized over non-AC base topoi.
Witness I provides the canonical countermodel to epimorphism splitting.
Non-AC lattices measure the strength of theorems when Axis I choice is dropped.
Higher choice AC_(n,m) generalizes Axis I choice to higher homotopy levels.
The Choice-Geometry Residuum Atlas unifies all Axis I choice results.
Splitting the large skeletal inclusion Card -> Set shifts Axis I equivalence-splitting one universe upward to Global Choice.
Base-topos logic deforms fiber subobject classifier geometries.
Witness I separates two-valuedness Sub(1) = 2 from external projectivity.
Intermediate logics and pointfree topologies form core non-AC lattices.
Classical Boolean clamping 1 + 1 -> Omega closes the constructive Omega^X / 2^X gap in double-clamped Set_ZFC.
Witness III step-product relies on rank-omega infinite product towers.
Witness V Cantor tail quotient Q_E0 originates from biproduct-tail cokernels.
Categorical Big Five and W-types depend on arithmetic infinity calibrations.
Smallness of the natural numbers object N in S supplies the arithmetic infinity clamp in Set_ZFC.
Lambek's Lemma (lambek_isIso from Chapter 3 Section 3.7) underpins the structural membership isomorphisms on mu P_S and nu P_S.
Witness II anchors Axis IV delta-ring lift torsors and slice perfection.
Witness IV directed facet cycles erect combinatorial characteristic obstructions.
Witness III provides the primary non-invertible higher category phantom.
Witness IV establishes the non-invertible directed cubical amalgamation obstruction.
Witness V models smooth 4-manifold directional end-quotients.
Higher cell invertibility governs Postnikov stepwise gerbe vanishing.
Axis V directional invertibility stratifies the four-tier (inf, inf)-ladder.
Higher groupoid loop groups Omega(nu P_Anima, [q, q]) ~= Z/2Z directly unite Axis V with Axis VII.
Two-axis relativization provides the framework for base-fiber conservation.
Witness V exhibits the non-splitting light condensed class Ext^1_CondAb.
Double-Solvent Theorem analyzes the light condensed E_0 tail quotient underlying radial 4-manifold smoothings.
Base-Fiber Conservation explains why Felgner L_in-conservativity over ZFC shatters into Glazer's leak when Replacement is dropped.
Axis VI direct-image descent exists_g promotes P_S to the covariant endofunctor whose fixed points mu P_S and nu P_S define Axis VII.
Failure of Axis VI Replacement in V_(omega+omega) precipitates countable colimit escape and breaks class-to-set flatness.
Axis VI image descent and Power Set form the upper size-compression clamps and frame the Borel determinacy pincer.
Relaxing Aczel bisimulation and (-1)-truncation along Axis VII uncovers Boffa Quine torsors and nu P_Anima loop fossils.
Axis VII Foundation (Coalg_wf(P_S) -> Coalg(P_S) with nu^wf P_S ~= mu P_S < nu P_S) and hereditary (-1)-truncation form the lower structural clamps of Set_ZFC.
T_odd is the primary witness in the Choice-Geometry Residuum Atlas.
Nominal parity cohomology anchors Kihara's atomic choice spectrum.
Rieger-Bernays permutations of infinite Quine atoms Q_0 realize Cont(Sym(Q_0)) ~= Nom with slice twin [Q_0^(2)] and parity [T_odd(Q_0)] torsors.
R_2 and DualInt are formally verified in DeltaRingPerfection.lean.
The step-product phantom refutes Conjecture C1 and separates Tier 1 from Tier 2.
F_n cycles prove the cubical n >= 3 disjoint amalgamation impossibility.
Q_E0 and UHF(2^inf) form the core invariant of the Double-Solvent Theorem.
Cantor space 2^N Borel complexity connects H(aleph_1) pointillist continuum failure to Martin's proper-class unraveling coalgebra.
Non-AC continuum and exactness theorems ground Lean formalization checks.
Higher choice bounds establish Core Conjecture 4 (Postnikov Stepwise).
The choice atlas grounds Core Conjectures 1, 2, and 3.
Choice residuums are formalized in NominalSimplicity and InfinityResiduum.
Atomic choice and Fraïssé topoi open Horizons III and IV (Problems 9.5-9.8).
Stabilization in CatSp is defined across the four tiers of the ladder.
State-coalgebraic rank separation and the step-product phantom witness are formalized in OrdinalRankCompleteness.lean and StepProductPhantom.lean.
The four-tier (inf, inf)-localization ladder directly grounds Open Problems 9.11 (Horizon VI) and 9.16 (Horizon VIII class calibration).
Cubical amalgamation walls are formalized in CubicalAmalgamation.lean.
Cubical phase transitions open Open Problems 9.7 and 9.8.
The 5 core conjectures define the theoretical targets for the 17 open problems.
CatSp stabilization barriers lead directly to Open Problem 9.12.
Double-Solvent core invariants (ZFC splitting, coset density, continuous T1 blindness) are formally verified in BorelTailResiduum.lean.
Double-Solvent bounds lead directly to Open Problem 9.13 (exotic R^4 moduli).
Combining upper/lower ZFC clamps with Card -> Set equivalence-splitting pins down the NBG class envelope and Classical.choice gate.
Vertical class hierarchies and pi_Set non-conservativity pose Open Problems 9.16 and 9.17 in Horizon VIII.
Quotienting Boffa twin torsors and multiset loop groups maps directly to Lean's propext + Quot.sound ZFSet quotient gate.
Decalage from terminal univalent multisets nu P_Anima to Rieger-Bernays permutation topoi forms Open Problem 9.17.
Chapter 7's universe clamps are machine-checked in the tenth production module HomotopyCRM/SetsResiduum.lean (1,401 lines, 19 checks).
Martin's proper-class Borel unraveling coalgebra and double-clamped scale-invariance launch Horizon VIII (Problems 9.15-9.17).
Formal verification provides the verified foundation for the Epilogue Thesis.
The open research horizons complete the master synthesis of CRM.
